headline: Xen Orchestra auth bypass and AhsayCBS flaws exploited; N-able keeps N-central offline after dozens of zero-days published

bullets.text: Changed: attackers are exploiting a critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra to hijack VM servers (BleepingComputer). The brief names no CVE or fixed release yet.
Changed: attackers are exploiting AhsayCBS flaws CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to deploy a sandbox-evading Python backdoor (The Hacker News).
N-able has taken its hosted N-central remote access service offline after a researcher published dozens of zero-days; the story now spans 4 outlets. No fixes are named yet.
Changed: AI company Fireworks says hackers stole data and billing information in October breaches; other reports say the exposure widened to incomplete model weights (5 outlets).
SSHole (OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158) exploitation continues (4 outlets). It is in CISA KEV with GPUStack CVE-2026-102895, FreeSwitch CVE-2026-116779 and IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2026-123218, all due 11-12.

Still active: Barracuda Email Security Gateway flaws are being exploited for root access; the brief names no CVEs or fixed releases. 300 malicious packages were listed in 7 days, mostly npm; the week ran 0.94x the 90-day average.

actions: Xen Orchestra: check the vendor advisory, update now, and restrict its web interface to admin networks until patched.
AhsayCBS: patch CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 and look for unexpected Python processes on backup servers.
Patch OpenSSH (CVE-2026-123158), GPUStack, FreeSwitch and IBM Aspera Faspex before the 11-12 KEV deadline.
N-central users: limit network exposure of N-central servers and agents, and watch N-able for fixes.
Fireworks and Qubole customers: rotate API keys and credentials shared with those services and review access logs.
Barracuda ESG: apply available fixes, restrict management access and check appliances for signs of root compromise.
